statement: Phelan Farm is a cool-climate coastal California project in Cambria, within the San Luis Obispo Coast wine context.
Greg Phelan planted several acres of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir on their own roots at the Cambria property in 2007.

scope_notes: CARTA records collaboration/work rather than an unsupported founder or owner edge for Raj Parr.
statement: Raj Parr was introduced to Greg Phelan in 2017 and subsequently worked with him to reshape the vineyard through new plant material and farming choices.
Phelan Farm's current vineyard map lists Mondeuse in the Jensen and Devine sections, alongside a broader set of cool-climate varieties.

scope_notes: Current producer-described practice, not a timeless certification claim.
statement: Phelan Farm describes no-till farming since 2007, livestock integration, natural farm-made preparations, no synthetic herbicides/fungicides, and no sulfur or copper use on the property.
Phelan Farm states that its wines ferment with natural yeast, see no sulfur in vineyard or cellar, age in older oak, and are hand-bottled without fining or filtration.
Phelan Farm Mondeuse is a varietal Mondeuse wine.

resolution_needed: Resolve whether the apparent difference reflects vintage-specific practice, a source error, or a change in protocol; do not encode a universal whole-cluster or destemmed rule.

source_refs.notes: Current importer says the single-parcel Mondeuse is always destemmed.

statement: Trade sources conflict on Phelan Farm Mondeuse stem use: a 2021 technical sheet describes whole-cluster fermentation, while a current importer description says the single-parcel Mondeuse is always destemmed.
TTB lists San Luis Obispo Coast (SLO Coast) as an American Viticultural Area established on March 9, 2022.
Domaine de Chevillard is led by Matthieu Goury, with Guillemette Renard materially involved in the estate and its plant-based vineyard preparations.
Domaine de Chevillard works in the Combe de Savoie, with core vineyard presence around Saint-Pierre-d'Albigny and Saint-Jean-de-la-Porte.

resolution_needed: Current first-party pages disagree between approximately 10 and 12 hectares; treat size as approximate and time-sensitive until the producer reconciles the figures.
statement: Current Domaine de Chevillard pages describe the estate as approximately 10 to 12 hectares rather than supporting one exact durable acreage figure.

scope_notes: The source documents conversion timelines; CARTA does not infer no-copper/no-sulfur practice or a biodynamic certification beyond what is stated.
statement: The domaine states that it entered organic conversion in 2017 and biodynamic conversion in 2020, while Guillemette Renard prepares plant-based vineyard treatments.
INAO publishes Vin de Savoie Apremont as an AOP product within the Savoie / Vin de Savoie appellation framework, where the appellation name may be complemented by approved commune names.
Domaine de Chevillard identifies Apremont as a white AOP Savoie cru in its range and presents Jacquère as the estate's principal local white-grape context for Apremont/Abymes wines.
The domaine describes indigenous-yeast vinification, restrained wood use, and a release rhythm in which wines spend roughly a year in barrel and a year in bottle before sale.
Chevillard's local Savoie grape set prominently includes Jacquère, Altesse and Mondeuse, with its Roussette de Savoie wine identified as Altesse.
Rafael López de Heredia y Landeta began planning and building the Haro bodega in 1877 after learning from French wine merchants working in Rioja.
R. López de Heredia Viña Tondonia is based in Haro, in Rioja Alta.

scope_notes: Context for the producer, not a claim that every current wine is sourced from every named vineyard.
statement: The estate describes Viña Tondonia as planted in 1913-1914 and lists Viña Cubillo, Viña Bosconia and Viña Zaconia among its other historic vineyard holdings.
Recent Viña Gravonia technical sheets identify the wine as 100% Viura.

scope_notes: Technical practice documented across recent vintages; CARTA does not treat Rioja law as requiring egg-white fining.
statement: Recent Viña Gravonia technical sheets document fermentation in large oak vats, four years of oak aging with two rackings per year, fresh egg-white fining, and unfiltered bottling.

resolution_needed: Confirm the formal historic/current naming relationship between Viña Gravonia and Viña Zaconia from first-party estate documentation before creating a vineyard identity or name assertion.
statement: A recent trade technical sheet describes Viña Gravonia as sourced from the Zaconia vineyard, while the estate's own site separately lists Viña Zaconia among its historic vineyards; the exact Gravonia/Zaconia vineyard-name crosswalk remains unresolved.
The Consejo Regulador DOCa Rioja states that Viura is also known as Macabeo.
Hofgut Falkenstein is a family-scale Saar Riesling estate in the Mosel wine region run by Erich Weber and his son Johannes Weber around Niedermennig.

scope_notes: Specific practices are recorded instead of asserting organic or biodynamic certification.
statement: Importer documentation describes the Webers as eschewing herbicides and artificial fertilizers and using cow manure in the vineyards.
Hofgut Falkenstein ferments with ambient/native yeasts, uses old 1000-liter fuder for many Rieslings, and bottles many lots cask by cask.

scope_notes: Cask names and AP numbers are vintage/lot identifiers attached to the durable wine identity, not separate vintage wine entities.
statement: Hofgut Falkenstein produces a Niedermenniger Sonnenberg Riesling Kabinett trocken; a 2024 example is identified as the Munny cask and AP 9.

scope_notes: AP means Amtliche Prüfungsnummer, an official quality-test number; it is not itself a cask number.
statement: German Wine Act §20 treats Kabinett as a Prädikat, requires an official Amtliche Prüfungsnummer for Prädikatswein, and provides that Kabinett is awarded only where enrichment was not performed.
Villalobos is a family wine project in Lolol, Colchagua Valley, led by the Villalobos family; trade documentation identifies Enrique Villalobos and Rita Encina among its principals.

scope_notes: CARTA does not characterize these 1940s-era vines as pre-phylloxera or as having 'survived phylloxera.'
statement: Villalobos describes Viñedo Silvestre as an approximately 80-year-old Carignan vineyard kept wild for decades, without pruning or irrigation, with vines growing among native Chilean vegetation.
Villalobos places Viñedo Silvestre in Lolol, Colchagua Valley, about 30 km from the Pacific coast and around 100 metres above sea level.

Viñedo Silvestre is documented as 100% Carignan, hand-picked, spontaneously fermented with native yeast in stainless steel, unpressed, unfined and unfiltered, then aged 18 months in old neutral French oak after spontaneous malolactic fermentation.

scope_notes: The interview supports direct practical support/collaboration, not a formal employment or mentorship hierarchy.
statement: The Villalobos family says it began making a small amount of wine in 2007 with support from their friend Mathieu Rousseau.
Château Simone is in Meyreuil, about four kilometres from Aix-en-Provence, and has been in the Rougier family since 1830.
Château Simone describes its vineyard on the north-facing slopes of the Massif du Montaiguet in a protected bowl crossed by the Arc river, on limestone scree with clay, pebbles and gravel.

scope_notes: This is a practice claim, not an assertion of continuous organic certification since the nineteenth century.
statement: Château Simone says the vineyard was rebuilt after phylloxera, includes parcels over 125 years old, and is cultivated with soil tillage without weedkillers or chemical fertilizers.

scope_notes: Current producer technical formula; CARTA does not infer that historical vintages used identical percentages.
statement: The current Château Simone Blanc technical sheet lists 80% Clairette, 10% Grenache Blanc, 5% Bourboulenc, 3% Ugni Blanc and 2% Muscat Blanc.
Château Simone Blanc is hand-harvested, fermented with native yeasts and matured in small oak for 18 months, including six months on fine lees, before bottling after a year in barrel.
INAO describes Palette as an AOP covering Aix-en-Provence, Meyreuil and Le Tholonet in a limestone-dominated Arc-river cirque, with white wines made predominantly from Clairette.

scope_notes: INAO supports a close historical relationship without requiring the stronger claim that Château Simone 'single-handedly' created Palette.
statement: INAO states that Palette's history is closely tied to Château Simone and that the Rougier family sought the origin designation obtained in 1948 for a wider set of nearby hamlets and estates.
